sources.title: George Lusztig, Lectures on Hecke Algebras with Unequal Parameters (MIT Fall 1999 lecture notes, arXiv:math/0108172v1), 84-page PDF
sources.locator: Sections 1.1-1.11 (PDF pp. 1-7), 2.1-2.5 (pp. 6-8), 3.1-3.5 (pp. 8-10) and 4.1-4.4 (pp. 10-11); every proof in those ranges was read in the extracted full text, with Theorem 1.9 and Proposition 3.3 checked line by line

contents.name: Sections 1.1-1.2: Coxeter matrices, the presented group W, the sign character, length, and l(sx)=l(x) plus or minus 1
contents.reason: The presentation, sign character and length function are the content of the HH-11 pair of this run, scaffolded by batch 2; this page consumes them from there and adds only the Hecke parameters.

contents.name: Proposition 1.3 and Corollary 1.4: the geometric representation, the exact order of ss', and reducedness with distinctness of the alternating words 1_k, 2_k
contents.reason: The rank-two order and the ambient reducedness of alternating words are proved by the dihedral item of the HH-11 pair, which this page's length-operator lemma consumes as its supplier.

contents.name: Propositions 1.5-1.7: the signed reflection action U_s(eps,t)=(eps(-1)^delta(s,t), sts), inversion sets of reduced expressions, and exchange
contents.reason: The signed action, inversion-set expression independence and exchange are the HH-11 pair's items; this page uses only the exchange statement, through the HH-11 exchange item declared as a dependency.

contents.name: 1.8 and Theorem 1.9 with proof: the graph X and braid connectivity of reduced expressions (Matsumoto)
contents.reason: Matsumoto's theorem is the HH-11 pair's item of this run (batch 2); this page consumes it to make the reduced products T_w well defined and does not reprove it.

contents.name: Proposition 1.10 with proof: l(swt)=l(w) and l(sw)=l(wt) imply sw=wt
Sections 2.1-2.5: Bruhat order and its subword characterisation with Corollary 2.5
contents.reason: Bruhat order and the subword criterion belong to the planned bruhat-subword page of this run; the Hecke items here use only Proposition 1.10 from this circle of ideas.

contents.name: Section 3.1: weight functions, the constraint L(s)=L(s') for finite odd m(s,s'), and determination of L by its values on S
Section 3.2(a): the algebra H presented by the quadratic relations (T_s-v_s)(T_s+v_s^{-1})=0 over A=Z[v,v^{-1}]
Section 3.2: T_w defined as the product along a reduced expression, well defined by Theorem 1.9
Section 3.2: the length-multiplication rules T_sT_w = T_sw (increasing) and T_sw+(v_s-v_s^{-1})T_w (decreasing)
Section 3.2: the spanning statement that {T_w} generates H as an A-module
Proposition 3.3, proof: the free module E with basis e_w and the operators P_s, Q_s defined by the two length cases
Proposition 3.3, proof: the six-case verification of P_sQ_t = Q_tP_s, including the two exceptional cases that force L(s)=L(t)
Proposition 3.3, proof: the quadratic and braid relations for the operators, and P_{s_1}...P_{s_k}e_1 = e_w for reduced expressions
Proposition 3.3: the evaluation A -> E at e_1, the transported algebra structure, the homomorphism H -> E and the independence of {T_w}
Section 3.4: the unique involutive anti-automorphism of H with T_s -> T_s, carrying T_w to T_{w^-1}
Section 3.5: the unique algebra involution with T_s -> -T_s^{-1}, carrying T_w to sgn(w)T_{w^-1}^{-1}
contents.reason: This pair uses only the reversal anti-automorphism of 3.4; the sign-twisted involution of 3.5 is consumed by no item of the standard-basis, bar, normalization or example set, so it is not built here.

contents.name: Section 4.1: invertibility of T_s with T_s^{-1} = T_s-(v_s-v_s^{-1})
Section 4.2: the coefficient involution v -> v^{-1} and the bar homomorphism with T_s-bar = T_s^{-1} and T_w-bar = T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}
Section 1.11: irreducibility, tameness, and the finite/integral/affine trichotomy
contents.reason: The classification of tame and affine Coxeter systems is the planned affine-diagrams page of this run; the Hecke standard-basis items need none of it.
